slides.title: One track on your wall, like a work in a museum.
slides.text: An e-ink frame that hangs a single track from 320kbps.club: its cover and liner notes on a museum label, over a map of where the artist comes from.
slides.alt: Liner showing Thomas Bangalter, over a map of Paris, France

slides.title: One track, then nothing else.
slides.text: A new track every morning and evening. No feed to scroll, no autoplay: something to look at for a whole day, and to go and listen to.
slides.alt: Liner showing Balthazar, over a map of Belgium, Kortrijk circled

slides.title: Picked by a person, never an algorithm.
slides.text: Every track comes from 320kbps.club, where each one is chosen by hand. Follow the whole site, the track of the day, a curator or a playlist.
slides.alt: Liner showing Agnes Obel, over a map of Denmark, Gentofte circled

slides.title: Where the artist comes from.
slides.text: Where they were born or formed, not where they live now: Magugu is from Nigeria, even if based in the UK. No known origin, no picture.
slides.alt: Liner showing Magugu & Le Motel, over a map of Nigeria

slides.title: Drawn for six inks.
slides.text: Black, white, yellow, red, blue, green. Text without smoothing, a map that snaps to the pixel; only the cover is dithered.
slides.alt: Liner showing The Verve, over a map of the United Kingdom, Wigan circled

slides.title: Every picture, free to keep.
slides.text: Each track the frame hangs also becomes a 4K wallpaper and a black and white picture, free to download from the gallery.
slides.alt: Liner's black and white version of Thomas Bangalter, for a two-ink panel

slides.title: Small, open, yours to build.
slides.text: A Raspberry Pi Zero, a Spectra 6 panel, any frame with a mat. About €100 of parts, an afternoon, the MIT License.
slides.alt: Liner showing The Bamboos, over a map of Australia, Melbourne circled
